function.mechanism: Forms sulfite/bisulfite reducing species that limit oxidation and can inhibit spoilage-related reactions; used as a preservative/antioxidant in food systems.

adi.basis: Temporary group ADI 0.7 mg SO2 equivalents/kg bw/day (2016) was withdrawn in 2022 follow-up; EFSA used MOE approach and identified safety concern at current exposure scenarios.

efsa.key_finding: Available toxicity database was inadequate to derive an ADI; temporary ADI withdrawn; MOE results indicated safety concern for several population groups.

fda.notes: GRAS with GMP restrictions: not used in meats; not in foods recognized as vitamin B1 source; not on fruits/vegetables intended to be served or sold raw/fresh.

adi.basis: Group ADI of 0-0.7 mg/kg bw for sulfites (as SO2-equivalent context), with later intake/evaluation entries in the WHO/JECFA database.

concerns.summary: Reviews and regulatory assessments indicate sulfites can trigger bronchial hyper-responsiveness/allergic-type reactions in sensitive individuals, especially asthma phenotypes.
EFSA follow-up used prolonged visual evoked potential latency data for benchmark-dose derivation and judged data gaps unresolved, supporting concern at high dietary exposures.
Experimental saliva microbiome work reported rapid shifts in viability/composition after sulfite preservative exposure at tested concentrations.
Recent in vitro/animal studies report oxidative-stress and ferroptosis-related toxicity signals (gastric cells, bone model), but dose relevance to regulated human dietary exposure remains uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2022 follow-up concluded sulfur dioxide/sulfites used as food additives do not raise a concern with respect to genotoxicity.

populations: multiple population groups at high-percentile exposure in EFSA scenarios
adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA MOE values fell below target for several groups in refined and MPL-based scenarios; JECFA database also notes potential ADI exceedance in high consumers.

risk_assessment.rationale: E221 remains permitted but with significant caveats: EFSA withdrew the temporary ADI and identified safety concern in exposure modeling, while JECFA retains a bounded group ADI and FDA allows use with explicit restrictions. Evidence supports concern without meeting high-tier triggers such as major-jurisdiction bans or IARC Group 2/1 classification.
key_factors: MOE-based safety concern under high exposure
JECFA ADI exists but high-consumer exceedance potential noted
